transcript.text: my washin mashine wont turn on at all no lights nothin

If there are no lights or signs of life at all, it’s usually a power supply issue rather than the washer controls.

Try these safe checks:

1. Check the socket
• Plug in something else you know works, like a lamp or phone charger.
• If that doesn’t work either, the socket/circuit is the problem.

2. Check your breaker/fuse box
• Look for a tripped breaker or an RCD/GFCI switch that has flipped off.
• Reset it once. If it immediately trips again when the washer is plugged in, stop using it—the machine or wiring may have a fault.

3. Unplug and replug the washer
• Unplug it for 5–10 minutes, then plug it directly into the wall socket (not an extension lead or power strip).
• Make sure the plug is fully seated and any wall switch is turned on.

4. Inspect the plug and cable
• Look for cuts, crushing, scorch marks, a loose plug, or a burning smell.
• If you see any damage, don’t plug it back in.

5. Check for water/leaks
• If water has reached the plug, socket, or underside of the machine, switch off power at the breaker and arrange repair.

If the outlet has power but the washer remains completely dead, likely causes include a failed power cord/filter, internal fuse, control board, or door/power switch. Those need an appliance technician—avoid opening it yourself, as washers can retain dangerous electrical charge even unplugged.

What brand/model is it, and does the wall socket work with another appliance?
dont know the brand or model its built in behind a cupboard door and the writing is worn off. the kettle works in the kitchen tho so the sockets are ok. all the switches in the fuse box are up

The kettle working means the kitchen has power, but the washing machine may be on a separate socket, fused spur, or RCD circuit.

Check around the unit for a separate appliance switch:

• Look in the cupboard next to it, under the sink, or on the wall above the worktop for a switch labelled washing machine, appliances, or a small switch with a fuse drawer.
• Make sure it is switched on. Turn it off, wait 30 seconds, then turn it back on.
• If it has a little fuse holder, don’t poke inside it while powered. A blown fuse is possible, but ideally have someone competent replace it with the exact same fuse rating.

If you can safely access the plug behind/next to the machine:
• Switch the wall outlet off first, then check the plug hasn’t worked loose.
• Do not pull the appliance out if it is heavy, fixed in place, or water hoses may be strained.

Also check whether there is a separate RCD/reset button on a socket, extension lead, or appliance switch—not every trip appears as an obvious switch “down” in the fuse box.

If the dedicated switch/socket has power but the washer has absolutely no lights, it likely needs an appliance repair engineer. Common internal faults are the mains filter, power supply/control board, or wiring.

Do not keep resetting breakers or use an extension lead to try to power it if there’s any burning smell, water leak, or signs of damage.

ok i looked and theres a row of switches above the worktop and one says washer and it was OFF. my flatmate must of turned it off when she was cleaning. i switched it back on and the machine has lights now and works!

Great — that explains it. The washer’s dedicated wall switch had simply been turned off.

If it happens again, check that switch first. You may want to let your flatmate know it controls the washing machine, or put a small label/tape reminder near it.
